# AgentOps

> Turns a codebase into a knowledge graph AI coding agents can query — scanning, hybrid search, curated gotchas/decisions, and library docs, exposed over MCP and self-hosted as a single open-core product (one Rust server, one Next.js frontend, no price gate).

This file concatenates AgentOps's full documentation in one place so an agent can load complete context in a single fetch. See [llms.txt](llms.txt) for the linked, unexpanded index.

---

## README

AgentOps scans a repository into a persistent knowledge graph — files, symbols, dependencies, and how they relate — so an AI coding agent doesn't re-derive context from scratch every session. On top of that graph it layers hybrid search (dense embeddings + lexical/BM25 + exact-name matching, personalized-PageRank graph expansion), a curated Gotchas/Decisions notes system for the tribal knowledge that never makes it into code comments, and CLS-inspired local consolidation that tunes retrieval to a repo's own graph.

All of it is exposed to AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, and anything else that speaks MCP) through one MCP server — up to 38 tools, depending on the surface and access mode — plus a REST API and a web UI for humans: team management, a repo connection wizard, an interactive graph viewer, a gotcha curation workspace, usage/token tracking, and a library/docs tracker (docbrain).

It's a single open-core product: one Rust server process, one Next.js frontend, no price gate, one required env var to self-host.

### Features

- Knowledge graph & search — AST-aware scanning (Python, JS/TS, Go, Rust, C++, C#), dependency graph, hybrid semantic + lexical search, interactive graph viewer with a centrality hotspot overlay. Optional rust-analyzer pass (`install --with-lsp`) for Rust macro invocations.
- Gotchas & decisions — a curation workflow for the "why": notes are matched to the symbols they're about, surfaced to agents automatically, and flagged stale when that symbol changes.
- Continuous indexing — GitHub App connections reindex on every push (clone → scan → embed → docgen); a tracked branch can be picked per connection.
- MCP for AI agents — one stdio binary (`agentops-mcp-server`) locally, or the authenticated `/mcp` endpoint on a hosted server. Read-only (`advisor`) by default; write tools are hidden entirely until an org switches to `full`.
- Library & docs tracking (docbrain) — registers dependencies, scrapes their docs at the installed version (including `llms.txt` where available), and makes them searchable.
- Usage & token tracking — per-session Claude Code token/cost totals, a ledger of AgentOps's own LLM spend, and offline session replay (`agentops usage`).
- Claude Code hooks (opt-in) — capture oversized tool output as searchable, redacted nodes; optionally compress noisy command output before it reaches context.
- Team management — orgs, fixed and custom roles, invites, per-repo access, audit log, multi-org switching. No external identity provider required.
- Local consolidation — at end_session, trains a small projection head on the repo's own graph locally, promoted only if it improves retrieval on a held-out split.

### Quick start: run the server

Four ways to self-host. Every method needs exactly one required value: AGENTOPS_SECRETS_MASTER_KEY (generate with `openssl rand -hex 32`).

**Docker (recommended)**: `cp .env.example .env` (fill in the master key), then `docker compose up`. The `app` service runs the API (:8420) and web UI (:3000); `marketing` serves the public site (:4321). `--profile postgres` adds a bundled Postgres (pgvector) code-graph store (SQLite is the default); `--profile caddy` adds a TLS reverse proxy.

**Classic (binary + terminal wizard)**: `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jesus-Glez60/agentops/main/install.sh | sh` then `agentops init`.

**PM2**: `cargo build --release --bin agentops-server`, `(cd apps/web && npm ci && npm run build)`, `pm2 start ecosystem.config.js`. Visit `/setup` on first run.

**Kubernetes**: raw manifests at deploy/k8s/ — copy secret.yaml.example to secret.yaml and fill in the master key first.

The first visitor to `/login` sets up the org and becomes Owner; signup is invite-only after that by default.

Optional server features: `AGENTOPS_DATABASE_URL` (Postgres code graph, needed for multi-tenant hosting); `AGENTOPS_GITHUB_APP_*` + `AGENTOPS_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (GitHub App connections + push reindex); `AGENTOPS_WEB_APP_URL` (browser-based CLI device login); `AGENTOPS_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` with optional `AGENTOPS_ANTHROPIC_MODEL`/`_MODEL_CHEAP` (LLM-assisted features — opt-in, everything else works without a key); `AGENTOPS_QDRANT_URL` (heavy BGE-M3 semantic search); `AGENTOPS_LINEAR_API_KEY` (Linear sync).

### Quick start: connect your coding tool

Against a hosted server, from inside the repo: `curl -fsSL https://<server>/connect.sh | sh`. It installs the CLI if needed and runs `agentops connect --remote <server> --device-login`: approve the device in a browser, a personal API key is minted, and the coding tool is pointed at the server's `/mcp` endpoint. By hand: `npx agentops-cli connect --remote https://<server>` (browser login by default, or `--api-key`). The connection is saved to `.context/agentops-remote.json`.

Solo, fully local: `npx agentops-cli install` (scan + AGENTS.md), then `npx agentops-cli connect` (local stdio MCP server + AGENTS.md/skills via Ruler).

Connect options: `--agents <ids>` (any Ruler-supported agent), `--global` (user-level skills/MCP; agents register repos themselves via `register_repo`/`scan_repo`), `--no-hooks` (Claude Code hooks are on by default) and `--compress-commands`, `--access-mode full` (expose write tools).

### CLI reference

- `install` — Scan a repo into the graph and generate AGENTS.md.
- `connect` — Connect a coding tool (local stdio MCP, or `--remote` hosted).
- `status` — Show what's currently scanned for a repo.
- `repos` — List every repo `agentops install` has run against on this machine.
- `forget` — Remove a repo from the local manifest (graph data untouched).
- `docgen` — Generate an onboarding/engineering doc (repo-map.md) from a scanned repo.
- `changelog` — What changed in a repo's code/notes across scans.
- `note` — Add a gotcha/decision/knowledge note, symbol-matched into the graph.
- `ingest-notes` — Recursively ingest a notes folder into a repo's graph.
- `search` — Search embedded symbols/notes; `--hybrid` adds lexical + exact-name signals, `--graph-expand` adds PageRank expansion.
- `explain` — Generate an LLM explanation of a symbol and record it as a Definition node.
- `watch` — Watch a repo and auto-rescan on file changes.
- `sync-docs` — Scan a repo's dependencies and auto-register any docbrain doesn't know about.
- `task` — Native tasks (create/list/update-status/close/activity/summarize/sync-linear).
- `usage` — `sync` Claude Code session token/cost totals (local or `--remote`); `report` replays sessions offline.
- `librarian` — `export-labels` then `dry-run` to evaluate cheap models (Anthropic or OpenAI-compatible) at cataloguing gotchas.
- `serve` — Run the stdio MCP server.
- `serve-api` — Run the merged REST API server.
- `docbrain-serve` — Run the docbrain-only stdio MCP server.
- `api-key` — Generate an instance-wide API key for the REST API's optional auth.
- `init` — Interactive first-run setup wizard for a classic terminal deployment.
- `migrate-graph` — One-off copy of a repo's SQLite graph into Postgres.

### Architecture

One Rust workspace (agentops-core/crates/*, docbrain-core/crates/*) builds `agentops-server` (merged REST API + `/mcp` + `/connect.sh`), `agentops-mcp-server` (unified stdio MCP server), and the `agentops` CLI. Two frontends: apps/web (Next.js, served under a configurable base path) and apps/marketing (Astro, site root). SQLite by default; Postgres (pgvector) for the code graph when AGENTOPS_DATABASE_URL is set. Embeddings run locally via ONNX.

A local server registers AgentOps as a docbrain library (metadata only) on boot — run `scrape_library` with `slug: agentops` once, then `search_docs`/`get_docs` work against AgentOps's own docs. Hosted org members do not see this entry (each org has its own docbrain store).

## REST API summary

Full detail in docs/openapi.yaml / docs/index.html. The merged server (agentops-server, default bind 127.0.0.1:8420) exposes ~100 routes:

- **Auth & sessions**: POST /auth/signup, POST /auth/login, POST /auth/login/2fa, GET /auth/bootstrap-status, GET/PATCH /auth/me, /auth/me/preferences|password|complete-onboarding, GET /auth/sessions, POST /auth/sessions/revoke-others, DELETE /auth/sessions/{id}, GET/POST /auth/api-keys, DELETE /auth/api-keys/{id}, POST /auth/2fa/enroll|confirm|disable, POST /auth/2fa/backup-codes/regenerate, POST /auth/logout, POST /bootstrap/config.
- **CLI device login (RFC 8628)**: POST /auth/cli/device (start), POST /auth/cli/device/approve (browser, session), POST /auth/cli/device/token (poll). GET /connect.sh serves the one-command connect script.
- **Team management** (session): GET /team, GET /team/members, PATCH/DELETE /team/members/{id}, GET /team/roles, POST /team/roles/custom, PATCH/DELETE /team/roles/custom/{key}, GET/PUT /team/mcp-access-mode, POST /team/transfer-ownership, POST /team/delete-organization, GET/POST /team/invites, POST /team/invites/{id}/resend, DELETE /team/invites/{id}, GET/PUT /team/repo-access, GET /team/audit-log, POST /invites/accept, GET /invites/{token}, GET /me/memberships, POST /me/switch-tenant.
- **Integrations** (session): GET /integrations, POST/DELETE /integrations/{provider}, GET /integrations/{provider}/oauth/start|callback, GET /integrations/me, POST/DELETE /integrations/me/{provider}.
- **Repositories & indexing** (session-or-api-key): POST /repos/connect, GET /repos, DELETE /repos/{id}, POST /repos/{id}/verify, POST /repos/{id}/attach-ssh|attach-github-app, POST /repos/{id}/index, GET /repos/{id}/index/status, POST /repos/{id}/index/retry, GET /repos/{id}/branches, PATCH /repos/{id}/branch, POST /repos/{id}/regenerate-key, GET /repos/github-app/install-url|callback|installations, GET /repos/github-app/installations/{id}/repos, POST /repos/github-app/installations/{id}/connect.
- **Search, graph & usage** (session-or-api-key, keyed by connection id): GET /local-search, POST /search/index, GET /search, POST /docs/search/index, GET /docs/search, GET /nodes, GET /scans, POST /repos/{name}/rescan, POST /repos/{name}/edges/{id}/reinforce, GET /repos/{id}/nodes/{node_id}, POST /repos/{id}/nodes/{node_id}/curation, GET /repos/{id}/nodes/{node_id}/graph, GET /repos/{id}/graph, GET /repos/{id}/docs, GET /repos/{id}/usage, POST /repos/{id}/usage/sync, GET /activity, GET /gotchas.
- **Tools (MCP-over-REST)** (api-key): GET /tools, POST /tools/{name}; GET /docbrain/tools, POST /docbrain/tools/{name}. **MCP over HTTP**: /mcp (session or personal API key only).
- **Libraries (docbrain)**: GET /docbrain/libraries, GET /docbrain/libraries/{slug}.
- **Webhooks** (HMAC-verified): POST /webhooks/github (push → reindex), POST /webhooks/linear. Linear task sync (session): GET/POST /linear/auto-kickoff, DELETE /linear/auto-kickoff/{team_id}, POST /linear/tasks/{task_id}/push-status|summarize.
- **Other**: GET /health (no auth), POST /contact-leads (marketing contact form).

## MCP tools summary

One MCP server — `agentops-mcp-server` over stdio, or `/mcp` on a hosted server. Write tools are hidden in `advisor` mode.

- **Repo & code graph**: status, register_repo, unregister_repo, scan_repo, list_scans, get_symbol, fetch_content, related_context, explain_symbol, get_changelog, local_semantic_search.
- **Notes**: list_gotchas, add_note, ingest_notes.
- **Docs & setup**: init_agents_md, generate_docs, persist_blueprint_doc.
- **Sessions & usage**: get_session, get_session_guide, end_session, report_usage.
- **Tasks**: create_task, list_tasks, update_task_status, get_task_activity.
- **Libraries (docbrain)**: list_libraries, get_library, discover_library, register_library, scrape_library, sync_changelogs, get_docs, search_docs, get_code_examples, list_changelog, get_job_status.
- **Heavy semantic tools** (only when AGENTOPS_QDRANT_URL is set): semantic_search, semantic_index, search_docs_indexed, index_docs_indexed.
